goal: Fix the application so every test in tests/test_acceptance.py passes. Do not edit that file; read the QA handover notes for the failing behaviour.

decisions.what: Made no code change; the current tree already passes every acceptance test
decisions.why: One full run on an otherwise idle machine passed every test, AC_42, AC_52 and AC_59 included, and the protected file's hash matches the verify command
decisions.evidence: python3 -m pytest -q --durations=15 -> 494 passed in 846.05s (/tmp/full.log); sha256sum tests/test_acceptance.py = 8127bf0d...0e05

decisions.what: Took the earlier attempts' failures to be agent timeouts and API errors, not failing tests
decisions.why: Runs 596 and 597 are recorded as timeouts at about 2400 s, runs 598 and 599 as network_error (API 502 upstream_unreachable), and none stored a test-failure output

assumptions: The speed-up that attempt 1 committed to app/business.py and app/rules.py (commit 7dc912b) is the fix this ticket needed; it is in the tree that now passes
open_questions: The full suite takes about 14 minutes (846 s), a large share of the 2400 s agent limit; QA and engineer tickets that must run it once are at risk of timing out

lessons.lesson: On a retried QA-fix ticket, first look in /logs/live.db (runs.outcome) and /live/runs/<run>/agent.stdout to see whether earlier attempts failed on tests or on timeouts or API errors. Then start the single full run early in the background: write to a /tmp log with a DONE marker and poll it with sleep loops.
lessons.when: Ticket retries whose earlier handovers have no output_tail
lessons.evidence: runs 596-599 were timeout and network_error; the suite passed with no change
